fields.Trigger: Monthly settlement cycle per consignment agreement

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "discounts shared per agreement" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews sell-through report" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-submit of "submits settlement statement to vendor" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-378 (ensure controlled execution — Consignment & VMI Settlement & Analytics (PA-45.3).)
- operational: AP Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Settlement disputes**: Vendor may dispute unit counts or deduction calculations; maintain detailed transaction-level sell-through data for audit support
- **Timing mismatch**: Sell-through period and payment period may not align; clear contractual settlement calendar prevents disputes
System Touchpoints: - Settlement statement generation and vendor portal submission (W1942.3)
- Integration with W7 (AP processing) for payment
Time Estimate: - 2–4 hours/month for review; payment processing absorbed in standard AP cycle

steps.activity: System generates monthly consignment sell-through report per vendor: (a) total units sold by SKU in settlement period, (b) consignment cost per unit per SKU, (c) total settlement amount: units sold × consignment cost, (d) deductions: (i) returns processed, (ii) damages charged to vendor per agreement, (iii) promotional discounts shared per agreement, (e) net settlement amount

AP Manager reviews sell-through report: (a) verify unit counts against POS transaction data, (b) verify consignment costs per agreement (any price changes applied correctly?), (c) verify deductions (returns, damages, promo contributions), (d) flag any discrepancies for Category Manager review

AP Manager submits settlement statement to vendor: (a) via vendor portal (preferred), (b) settlement statement includes: sell-through detail, deductions, net amount, payment terms (typically Net 30 from settlement date), (c) vendor reviews and confirms within 10 business days

Payment processing: (a) vendor invoice (settlement statement) processed through AP, (b) standard payment run per W7.9, (c) payment to vendor bank account, (d) GL posting: debit consignment AP (liability created at ownership transfer), credit cash/bank

fields.Participants: Category Manager, Pricing Analyst, VP Merchandising

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generates quarterly consignment margin report" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews margin analysis" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-378 (ensure controlled execution — Consignment & VMI Settlement & Analytics (PA-45.3).)
- operational: Category Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden costs**: Consignment may appear high-margin but operational costs (reconciliation, vendor management, aging management) reduce actual profitability; include operational overhead in margin analysis
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W85 (product costing & margin analysis) for consolidated margin view

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst generates quarterly consignment margin report: (a) gross margin % by consignment vendor, (b) gross margin % by consignment category (appliances, tiles), (c) compare consignment margin to owned-inventory margin for same categories, (d) margin trend: improving or declining by vendor, (e) identify vendors where consignment margin < owned-inventory margin by > 5 percentage points

Category Manager reviews margin analysis: (a) low-margin consignment vendors: negotiate improved consignment costs, (b) evaluate alternatives: can BuildRight purchase directly at better margin?, (c) high-margin consignment: consider expanding consignment range with vendor, (d) assess total value of consignment arrangement: (margin × volume) vs. (capital saved from not owning inventory)

Annual: Category Manager negotiates consignment cost adjustments with vendors based on: (a) volume commitment (higher volume = lower consignment cost), (b) competitive benchmarking (what margin do other retailers get?), (c) total relationship value (vendor also supplies non-consignment goods)

fields.Participants: VP Supply Chain, Category Manager, Finance Manager

workflows.name: VMI Inventory Carrying Cost & Optimization Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-calculate of "calculates VMI inventory carrying cost" (replaces manual Step 1).
Controls: - CTL-378 (ensure controlled execution — Consignment & VMI Settlement & Analytics (PA-45.3).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Attribution difficulty**: Hard to isolate VMI program impact from overall supply chain performance; need control group (similar non-VMI SKUs) for comparison
System Touchpoints: - VMI inventory analytics with carrying cost calculation (W1944.1)
- Integration with W35 (FP&A reporting) for carrying cost data

steps.activity: Finance Manager calculates VMI inventory carrying cost: (a) average VMI inventory value (at WAC) per month, (b) carrying cost rate: warehousing + insurance + obsolescence risk + cost of capital (~20–25% of average inventory value per year for Philippine retail), (c) compare VMI carrying cost to non-VMI carrying cost for similar SKUs

VP Supply Chain evaluates VMI optimization: (a) inventory turns: VMI SKUs vs. non-VMI SKUs in same category, (b) stockout cost: lost sales from VMI stockouts vs. non-VMI stockouts, (c) procurement labor savings: VMI auto-replenishment reduces Buyer workload by ~X hours/month, (d) overstock cost: excess VMI inventory carrying cost above max level

Recommendations: (a) VMI SKUs with high overstock: tighten max levels or remove from VMI, (b) VMI SKUs with frequent stockouts: increase min levels or add supplier, (c) high-performing VMI vendors: expand VMI scope to additional SKUs, (d) low-performing VMI vendors: consider converting to standard procurement per W1947

fields.Participants: VP Supply Chain, Category Manager, CFO
fields.Volume: Consolidated across all consignment & VMI operations

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "count, SKU count" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "VP Supply Chain reviews dashboard" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report to CFO and VP Merchandising" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-378 (ensure controlled execution — Consignment & VMI Settlement & Analytics (PA-45.3).)
- operational: VP Supply Chain review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data integration**: Consignment data (non-valuated) and VMI data (valuated) come from different inventory views; dashboard must consolidate both
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W35 (executive reporting) for consolidated view

steps.activity: Monthly dashboard generation: (a) consignment: total consignment inventory value (vendor-owned), sell-through rate, settlement accuracy, aging distribution, (b) VMI: total VMI inventory value (BuildRight-owned), fill rate, stockout rate, overstock rate, vendor compliance score, (c) combined: total consignment + VMI inventory as % of total inventory, total margin contribution, vendor count, SKU count
VP Supply Chain reviews dashboard: (a) identify trends, (b) flag exceptions for action, (c) distribute to Category Managers and Finance Manager

Quarterly: VP Supply Chain presents executive report to CFO and VP Merchandising: (a) program health: is consignment/VMI creating value?, (b) vendor performance: which vendors to expand, reduce, or terminate?, (c) financial impact: margin contribution, carrying cost, capital savings, (d) strategic recommendations

fields.Participants: Category Manager, VP Merchandising, VP Supply Chain, CFO, Vendor

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepares renewal analysis" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approves consignment terms from financial perspective" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-378 (ensure controlled execution — Consignment & VMI Settlement & Analytics (PA-45.3).)
- operational: Category Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Renewal gap**: If agreement expires without renewal, consignment goods status becomes ambiguous; set renewal calendar alerts 60 days before expiration
System Touchpoints: - Consignment vendor performance analytics for renewal support (W1946.1)
- Integration with W230 (legal contract review) for agreement documentation
Time Estimate: - 1–2 days preparation per vendor; negotiation varies

steps.activity: Category Manager prepares renewal analysis: (a) past year performance: sell-through rate, margin, return rate, (b) compare consignment arrangement vs. direct purchase alternative, (c) vendor relationship: payment timeliness, dispute resolution, support quality, (d) market conditions: are there alternative vendors offering better consignment terms?

Negotiation: (a) improved consignment cost (target 2–5% reduction annually), (b) expanded SKU range (add high-demand items to consignment), (c) improved terms: faster settlement, better damage responsibility allocation, (d) performance incentives: volume-based consignment cost reduction
CFO approves consignment terms from financial perspective: (a) margin impact, (b) balance sheet impact (consignment stock is off-balance-sheet — vendor-owned), (c) settlement terms cash flow impact

fields.Participants: VP Supply Chain, Category Manager, VP Merchandising
fields.Trigger: VMI vendor consistently underperforming; strategic decision to internalize replenishment

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-forecast of "forecasting risk" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-notify of "notify vendor of VMI termination per contractual notice period" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-378 (ensure controlled execution — Consignment & VMI Settlement & Analytics (PA-45.3).)
- operational: VP Supply Chain review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Transition disruption**: Switching from VMI to internal replenishment may cause temporary stock level instability; plan transition during low-demand period
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W2A (auto-replenishment) for new parameter setup

steps.activity: VP Supply Chain identifies VMI vendor for conversion: (a) fill rate consistently < 93% (below 97% target for 2+ quarters), (b) stockout frequency impacting sales, (c) vendor unable or unwilling to improve, (d) internal replenishment capability available (Buyer capacity, demand planning tools)

Decision analysis: (a) cost of conversion: additional Buyer labor, demand planning tool cost, (b) benefit of conversion: better fill rate, lower stockout, more control over replenishment timing, (c) risk of conversion: loss of vendor collaboration, BuildRight bears forecasting risk, (d) present business case to VP Merchandising

If approved: (a) transition VMI SKUs to standard procurement per W2A, (b) establish ROP/EOQ parameters per W312, (c) notify vendor of VMI termination per contractual notice period, (d) monitor first 90 days closely for service level impact

steps.activity: System identifies cross-entity consignment/VMI transactions: (a) consignment goods received by BuildRight Logistics DC but sold by BuildRight Depot store, (b) VMI stock at BuildRight Logistics DC transferred to BuildRight Depot stores, (c) ownership transfer revenue and COGS must be allocated to correct entities

AP Manager processes IC settlement for consignment/VMI: (a) consignment settlement: vendor payment from BuildRight Depot (selling entity), IC service fee from BuildRight Logistics (DC storage/service), (b) VMI settlement: standard PO payment from purchasing entity, IC transfer pricing for stock movements between entities, (c) post IC AP/AR per W14

Monthly IC reconciliation: (a) verify consignment/VMI IC balances match across entities, (b) resolve timing differences (sale in one entity, settlement in another), (c) elimination entries for consolidation per W9A

fields.Frequency: Continuous audit trail; annual documentation review
fields.Participants: Accounting Manager, Internal Auditor, External Auditor

workflows.name: Consignment & VMI Audit Trail & Compliance Documentation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documented with reason codes and approvals" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "verify consignment stock is correctly classified" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-378 (ensure controlled execution — Consignment & VMI Settlement & Analytics (PA-45.3).)
- operational: must strictly enforce non-valuated treatment
Pain Points / Risks: - **Balance sheet misclassification**: If consignment stock is inadvertently valued (treated as owned), it inflates inventory on balance sheet; system must strictly enforce non-valuated treatment
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W21 (internal audit) for audit coverage

steps.activity: System maintains continuous audit trail: (a) consignment: receipt → display → sale → ownership transfer → settlement, with timestamps, user IDs, and system references, (b) VMI: data sharing → replenishment → receipt → auto-confirmation → payment, with full traceability, (c) adjustments: damage, shrinkage, returns — all documented with reason codes and approvals

Annual: Accounting Manager prepares consignment & VMI documentation for external audit: (a) consignment inventory is vendor-owned — excluded from BuildRight's balance sheet inventory; provide vendor ownership documentation, (b) VMI inventory is BuildRight-owned — included in balance sheet at WAC; provide VMI agreement terms for audit review, (c) settlement reconciliation: consignment settlements matched to sell-through, VMI payments matched to GR, (d) provide sample of transactions for auditor testing

Internal audit of consignment & VMI per W21: (a) verify consignment stock is correctly classified (not inadvertently included in owned inventory valuation), (b) verify VMI stock levels per physical count, (c) test settlement accuracy on sample basis, (d) review vendor agreements for compliance with BuildRight policies
